1.why: Four options name conventional catalogue facets (marble, year, room, colour); 'the hand that wrote their register entries' is the odd, detective-flavoured one, so I bet the surprising facet.

2.why: [hedged-bet] Only option that both asserts a trend and declines to adjudicate its cause; the other four are single clean claims.

3.why: Most specific of the five and the only piecework rate, which fits a passage elsewhere conceding he 'paid her so little'.

4.why: The survey passage's other items turn on dates coming forward, and A is the only change that acts on when the season starts.

5.why: B/D/E are bare mental states and A is a near-paraphrase of C; C is the single concrete observable, so I bet the concrete one.

6.why: [hedged-bet] Unique decline-to-adjudicate option against two extremes (sure it is wrong / indifferent) and one warm-feeling distractor.

7.why: [hedged-bet] Only two-move concede-then-narrow option among four single-move absolutes; function questions key on the two-move option.

8.why: Matches the sibling item whose key-shaped option is 'a group taken from moulds made off other casts' — D is the firm-side statement of the same misconduct.

9.why: [hedged-bet] Unique 'unwilling to say whether anybody was at fault' against four committed stances; betting the decline.

10.why: A and B are a stove-pair trap and C/D are disposals; E is the most specific retention detail in a passage that turns on letters being kept.

11.why: Only option carrying a purpose clause ('laid to a fall toward a drain'), and a swept, drained floor explains the sibling item's 'why so little came out of the floor'.

12.why: Obvious-sense trap 'reply to' is present, so the key is the displaced sense; 'correspond to' is the standard literary displacement of 'answer to'.

13.why: Modern senses (idle pastime, freedom from employment) are the traps; 'ample time' is the displaced sense.

14.why: C and E are a direct reversal pair (shut from outside vs in daily use); betting the more loaded, more specific member.

15.why: Only do-nothing option and the only one carrying an author-voice reason clause; coheres with the memorial passage's attitude item, which holds the parishes wrong.

16.why: The only two-phase structural finding (walls one date, vault later), the shape this passage's other items prefer.

17.why: Only option naming a motive/attitude (the narrator's distrust) rather than a plot fact.

18.why: [hedged-bet] Unique reluctance-to-say option against four committed feelings.

19.why: Most specific and most human grievance among four procedural or material complaints.

20.why: 'unadorned'/'ordinary' are the obvious senses and therefore traps; 'candid' is the displaced sense.

21.why: 'able to be heard' is the obvious trap; in a passage about a record, the displaced sense is 'reliable'.

22.why: C and E are a parallel 'includes a group...' pair; C matches the firm-side item I also keyed to casts moulded off other casts.

23.why: [hedged-bet] Only option that withholds a verdict; the other four name a definite emotion.

24.why: [hedged-bet] Only negatively-qualified 'not by itself' option against four positive causal claims — the cautious-scientist shape this passage uses elsewhere.

25.why: Only option whose motive points at a third party (the addressee); the other four are all about Ottilie's own character.

26.why: Hedged option C exists but is overridden: the passage's recommendation item keys to 'leave it alone', so the author holds a firm view — E is the concede-they-mean-well-but-wrong fit.

27.why: [hedged-bet] Only unsettled/disputed option against four options that assert something settled or recorded.

28.why: A and E are a reversal pair (assumed yes vs expected no); given she refused, the ironic key is that he took it for granted.

29.why: 'a place in which business is done' is the obvious trap; 'a proper function' is the displaced sense of 'office'.

30.why: [hedged-bet] Only still-unsure option against four settled retrospective judgements.
